title: A page served over https dials wss://, not ws://
body:
## Summary
The page hard-coded ws://, so served over https by a relay (RelayTransport documents wss://relay.example) its socket was mixed content and never opened.

## Description
companion/index.html:172 (before) `new WebSocket('ws://' + location.host + '/ws')`. Over LAN the TV serves the page over http, so ws:// is right; tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt:32 documents the production relay as wss:// and says the phone page is served by the relay or a CDN, and tools/relay-stub.mjs serves the same file at /. Fixed: the scheme follows location.protocol.

## Flow
- open the pen page at https://relay/?pin=1234
- before: the browser blocks ws://relay/ws as mixed content; the pen shows "reconnecting" forever
- after: it dials wss://relay/ws

## Expected impact
The relay path can work in production. LAN behaviour unchanged (guard case).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the pen connects when served over https
Before: https page dials ws://relay.test/ws
After: https page dials wss://relay.test/ws; http/file page still ws://
Method: gate - tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs https case (route-fulfilled origin, fake socket) red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
companion/index.html:172 (before) `const sock = (ws = new WebSocket('ws://' + location.host + '/ws'));`
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt:32 `e.g. wss://relay.example/tv?session=abc`
red run: FAIL https: a page served over https dials wss:// (ws://relay.test/ws)

title: Every pen control has a name a screen reader can say
body:
## Summary
The five colour swatches were empty buttons, the tag cancel a lone "✕", and the tag input and scrub range had no label.

## Description
companion/index.html:110-114 (before) swatches carried only a background colour and aria-pressed; companion/index.html:94 tagcancel text "✕"; :92 tagtext placeholder only; :147 scrub no label. WCAG 4.1.2 (name, role, value); registry accessibility / name-and-description-wiring. Fixed with aria-labels (Yellow, Red, Cyan, Green, White; Cancel; Name tag; Position in the clip). Nothing visible changes.

## Flow
- a screen-reader user focuses a swatch
- before: "button, pressed"; after: "Yellow, toggle button, pressed"

## Expected impact
The ink colour, cancel and scrub become operable without sight.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every control has a spoken name
Before: 8 buttons/inputs with no letter or digit in aria-label, text or title
After: 0
Method: gate - new a11y check in tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs, red (8) before, green (0) after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
companion/index.html:110 `<button class="swatch" data-color="#FFD400" aria-pressed="true" style="background:#FFD400"></button>` (before)
red run: 8 unnamed <input id="tagtext"... | <button id="tagcancel"...>✕ | 5 swatches | <input id="scrub"...>

title: A locked-out phone is told to wait, not to type the PIN again
body:
## Summary
Every refusal read "<reason> · type the PIN from the TV", including "too many wrong PINs", during which the right PIN is refused too.

## Description
companion/index.html:195 (before) appended the same remedy to every reason. On "too many wrong PINs" PairingDesk refuses every hello for COOLDOWN_MS (30 s); since f0189837 that applies on LAN too. The copy prescribed a remedy that cannot help. Fixed: the locked reason says "wait half a minute, then type the PIN".

## Flow
- a phone is refused "too many wrong PINs"
- the viewer types the right PIN at once
- before: refused again, no explanation; after: the status said to wait

## Expected impact
The viewer is not refused twice for doing what the page told them.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the refusal copy prescribes a remedy that works
Before: locked status: "too many wrong PINs · type the PIN from the TV"
After: "too many wrong PINs · wait half a minute, then type the PIN"
Method: gate - new locked case in tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
companion/index.html:195 (before) `statusEl.textContent = (m.reason || 'not paired') + ' · type the PIN from the TV';`
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenConversation.kt PairingDesk.check LOCKED refuses the right PIN

title: The pad draws no ink before the TV welcomes the pen, and says why
body:
## Summary
While refused or reconnecting, send() dropped every message but the pad still echoed ink under the finger, so a stroke looked drawn and faded without reaching the TV.

## Description
companion/index.html:194 send() is a no-op unless connected, and the TV ignores input before a welcome; pointerdown (companion/index.html:345) still began a stroke and painted local echo. Tag and erase were lost the same way. Fixed: pointer-down does nothing while unpaired and the hint says why ("type the PIN above to draw" after a refusal, "not connected to the TV yet" otherwise); the welcome restores "draw here".

## Flow
- the TV refuses the PIN (or Wi-Fi drops)
- the viewer draws on the pad
- before: ink appears and fades, nothing on the TV; after: no ink, the hint explains

## Expected impact
The pad no longer pretends. Paired drawing unchanged (GUARD).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an unpaired pad does not show ink that goes nowhere
Before: 1745 ink pixels from a 10-move stroke after a refusal, no hint
After: 0 ink pixels, hint "type the PIN above to draw"; paired page still 2143 pixels
Method: gate - unpaired case and paired GUARD in tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
companion/index.html:194 `function send(o) { if (connected) ws.send(JSON.stringify(o)); }`
companion/index.html:345 pointerdown had no paired check
red run: FAIL unpaired: a stroke draws no ink and the pad says why (1745 ink pixels, hint "")

title: A spotlight preview shows the floor-sized ring the TV will draw
body:
## Summary
PenEngine floors a spotlight radius at 0.03 of the width; the phone preview drew the raw drag, so a short drag previewed a ring a tenth the size of the one that landed.

## Description
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt (spotlight `coerceAtLeast(0.03)`) vs companion/index.html previewShape (`Math.hypot(...)` only). Fixed: the preview applies the same floor; both sides name the constant (PenEngine.SPOTLIGHT_MIN_RADIUS, the page's SPOTLIGHT_MIN_RADIUS) and CompanionContractTest checks they agree. Coupled paths: PenEngine.kt (literal -> named constant, same value), CompanionContractTest.kt.

## Flow
- pick Spot, drag 2 px
- before: a 2 px ring under the finger, a 6%-of-width spotlight on the TV; after: the preview matches

## Expected impact
What the viewer sees while dragging is what lands.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the preview radius equals the committed radius
Before: preview ring 0.6% of the pad width vs 6.0% on the TV
After: 6.3% (floor plus line width); page constant seeded to 0.04 -> CompanionContractTest red
Method: gate - spotlight case in tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs red before, green after; seeded control on the contract check
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
core/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/core/PenEngine.kt:207 (before) `radius = metric.distance(msg.from, msg.to).coerceAtLeast(0.03)`
companion/index.html:401 (before) `ctx.arc(p1[0], p1[1], Math.hypot(p2[0] - p1[0], p2[1] - p1[1]), 0, Math.PI * 2)`
red run: ring 0.6% of the pad width, TV floor 6.0%

title: The scrub bar is a 32 px target, not 16 px
body:
## Summary
On a 375 x 667 phone every control is 36-40 px except the scrub range at the browser default 16 px, the only one under the 24 px WCAG 2.5.8 minimum and the one dragged with a thumb.

## Description
companion/index.html:60 styled the range with no height. Fixed: the range box is 32 px (track stays thin; the drawn-moment ticks stay centred, checked on a screenshot); the pad keeps 355 x 200.

## Flow
- open the page on a phone
- drag the scrub bar with a thumb
- before: a 16 px hit box; after: 32 px

## Expected impact
Fewer missed scrubs. 16 px more nav height on the phone; the pad did not shrink at 375 x 667.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every control meets the 24 px target minimum
Before: 1 of 25 nav controls under 24 px (Position in the clip 326x16)
After: 0 of 25
Method: gate - new target-size check at 375 x 667 in tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs, red before, green after
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
companion/index.html:60 (before) `input[type=range] { flex:1; accent-color:var(--ink); min-width:0; }`
probe: {"controls":25,"under44":25,"under24":1,"sample":[["Position in the clip",326,16]]}

title: live-ui-test check 15 looks for copy the page stopped saying
body:
## Summary
tools/live-ui-test.mjs:358 passes the wrong-PIN check only if the status matches /not paired/i, but since 0a6a553a the page says "wrong PIN · type the PIN from the TV", so the device run reports a refused intruder as a failure.

## Description
companion/index.html refusal copy changed in 0a6a553a from "not paired: <reason> — rescan the QR" to "<reason> · type the PIN from the TV"; "not paired" now appears only when the TV sends no reason, and PenConversation always sends one. The harness check reads copy, not state. Fix (in telestrator-harness, outside this round): assert on the bad class plus a visible PIN input (as tools/companion-refusal-test.mjs does), not on wording.

## Flow
- run tools/live-ui-test.mjs on the Stick
- check 15 opens ?pin=0000; the TV refuses with "wrong PIN"
- the regex /not paired/i fails on "wrong PIN · type the PIN from the TV"

## Expected impact
A device run stops reporting a working refusal as broken. Test-only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the device check passes for a refused intruder
Before: check 15 regex vs current copy: no match (FAIL predicted)
After: state-based check: PASS predicted
Method: simulation - the regex run against the page's current refusal string; the device run needs the Stick
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/live-ui-test.mjs:358 `check('a phone with the wrong PIN is refused', /not paired/i.test(intruderStatus), ...)`
0a6a553a^:companion/index.html `statusEl.textContent = 'not paired: ' + (m.reason || 'rejected') + ...`
companion/index.html now: `(m.reason || 'not paired') + ...`
instrument: out-of-scope (telestrator-harness): node -e running the check-15 predicate against the page's refusal status from companion-refusal-test; then the Stick run

title: The pairing PIN travels in the URL query, and the page writes it back there
body:
## Summary
The QR and the page carry the PIN as ?pin=, which a relay or proxy logs with the request line, and the page re-writes a typed PIN into the query with history.replaceState.

## Description
companion/index.html:163 reads `URLSearchParams(location.search).get('pin')`; the refusal form writes `q.set('pin', pin)` and history.replaceState. Over LAN the request goes to the TV; over a relay (tools/relay-stub.mjs serves the page at /) the GET line with the PIN reaches the relay's logs, which RelayTransport's doc says must learn nothing. Registry device-pairing / token-binding-and-transport: a URL fragment never leaves the client. Fix candidate: #pin= in the QR (tv-app PairingCard/Qr) and the page reading the fragment first, the query as a fallback.

## Flow
- scan the QR on a relay deployment
- the phone GETs /?pin=4821 from the relay
- the PIN is in the relay's access log

## Expected impact
The pairing secret stops leaving the living room. Needs the QR builder in tv-app; old QR codes keep working via the fallback.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the PIN is not sent to the page host
Before: PIN in the request line on every page load (query)
After: predicted: PIN only in the fragment, never sent
Method: simulation - request line walked for LAN and relay; the QR change is in tv-app
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
companion/index.html:163 `let pin = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get('pin') || '0000';`
companion/index.html pinbox submit `q.set('pin', pin); history.replaceState(null, '', '?' + q);`
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt:28 "The relay is dumb ... the PIN check ... never leave the device"
instrument: companion-refusal-test case: a page opened at #pin=<right> pairs and its location.search carries no pin; a tv-app unit test that the QR URL uses the fragment

title: A lost TV is redialled every second, forever, with no backoff
body:
## Summary
After a drop the page reconnects on a fixed 1 s timer with no ceiling, also while the phone screen is hidden, so a closed TV app costs 60 connection attempts a minute for as long as the tab lives.

## Description
companion/index.html:190 `setTimeout(connect, 1000)` on every non-refusal close; no backoff, no visibilitychange handling. RelayTransport (tv-app) already backs off to a ceiling; the phone does not. Fix candidate: exponential backoff from 1 s to ~15 s, reset on a welcome, and an immediate retry on visibilitychange to visible.

## Flow
- the viewer closes the TV app and leaves the phone on the page
- the page dials every second
- battery and Wi-Fi radio stay busy indefinitely

## Expected impact
Less battery and radio use when the TV is gone; a recovering TV is still picked up quickly. Risk: a slower reconnect after a long outage (mitigated by the visibility retry).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a missing TV costs a bounded number of attempts
Before: 60 connection attempts per minute, unbounded
After: predicted: about 8 per minute after the first minute
Method: simulation - timer walked; companion-refusal-test's fake TV can count attempts over 60 s on both arms
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
companion/index.html:190 `setTimeout(connect, 1000);`
tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt:68 backoff doubled up to MAX_BACKOFF_MS
instrument: companion-refusal-test case: a fake TV that never answers counts connections over 60 s (before ~60) and the drop case still pairs within 2 s

title: The page forbids pinch-zoom for the whole page
body:
## Summary
The viewport meta sets maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no, which blocks zoom on every control, not only on the drawing pad.

## Description
companion/index.html:5. WCAG 1.4.4 (resize text). The pad already has touch-action:none (companion/index.html:34), which is what keeps a drawing gesture from zooming; the page-wide ban also stops a low-vision viewer from enlarging the 11-12 px status and labels. Removing it may let a stray double-tap zoom the nav, which is a product call.

## Flow
- a low-vision viewer pinches the status line
- nothing happens

## Expected impact
Readable status and labels for low-vision viewers; possible accidental zoom on the nav.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - text can be enlarged
Before: zoom blocked page-wide
After: unmeasurable as a benefit without users; the mechanical part is a one-line meta change
Method: simulation - the pad's touch-action already isolates the gesture; the trade-off is taste
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
companion/index.html:5 `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no, viewport-fit=cover">`
companion/index.html:34 `touch-action:none;` on #pad
escalation: direction - accessibility vs accidental zoom on a one-handed remote

title: All 25 pen controls are under the 44 px touch guideline
body:
## Summary
At 375 x 667 every nav control is 36-40 px tall (swatches 40 x 36), below the 44 px platform guidance, on a page used one-handed while watching the TV.

## Description
Measured: 25 of 25 visible nav controls have a side under 44 px, 0 under 24 px after 61acf26f. Six rows of buttons share the space under a 355 x 200 pad. Raising them to 44 px costs ~36 px of height or the review/rate rows; which rows give way is a layout decision.

## Flow
- hold the phone in one hand, eyes on the TV
- reach for Undo or a swatch
- the 36-40 px targets are easy to miss

## Expected impact
Fewer mis-taps; the pad or a row loses space.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - controls meet the 44 px guideline
Before: 25 of 25 under 44 px
After: unmeasurable until the layout is chosen
Method: probe - Playwright bounding boxes at 375 x 667
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
escalation: direction - layout trade between pad height and control size
